analysis.investment_thesis: Awfis fails both legs of the Magic Formula — Earnings Yield of ~10% (EBIT ₹407 Cr / EV ~₹3,972 Cr) sits below the 12% threshold, and ROCE of 12.9% is well short of the 20%+ needed to call this a "good business." A capital-intensive lease-arbitrage model carrying ₹1,451 Cr in borrowings on ₹499 Cr equity does not qualify as a high-ROIC compounder at any price.
key_strengths: Revenue scaling rapidly — 41% CAGR over 6 years, ₹154 Cr → ₹1,208 Cr
FCF turning positive: ₹163 Cr in FY25 after years of cash burn, OCF positive 5/5 years
High gross margins (82%) suggest strong unit economics at the seat level
key_risks: ROCE only 12.9% — well below Magic Formula's 20% floor; business consumes capital faster than it earns on it
Debt spiral risk: borrowings ₹1,451 Cr (D/E 2.91), finance costs CAGR 73% vs revenue CAGR 41%
Single year of profitability (FY25 net profit ₹68 Cr) after six consecutive loss years — far too thin a track record
red_flags: Earnings Yield ~10% and ROIC 12.9% — both metrics fail Magic Formula thresholds simultaneously
Promoter holding at just 17% — dangerously low skin in the game
IND-AS 116 lease capitalisation inflates EBITDA (₹456 Cr) and operating income, masking the true cost of occupancy obligations
Finance costs rose from ₹5 Cr (2019) to ₹136 Cr (2025) — 73% CAGR — outpacing revenue growth
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Magic Formula verdict is quick: EV = Market Cap ₹2,592 Cr + Debt ₹1,413 Cr − Cash ₹33 Cr = ~₹3,972 Cr. EBIT (Operating Income) FY25 = ₹407 Cr → Earnings Yield ≈ 10.2%, below the 12% attractiveness threshold. ROCE reported at 12.9% — well under the 20% hurdle. The business fails both filters simultaneously, which the Magic Formula treats as a hard pass. The high EBITDA margin is an accounting artifact of IND-AS 116, which capitalises leases and pushes rent expense below the EBITDA line; strip that out and the underlying economics look far less impressive.

The structural problem is the business model itself: Awfis leases space on long contracts and subleases short — classic real estate arbitrage. This generates operating leverage in upcycles but destroys ROIC because the balance sheet keeps bloating (assets: ₹509 Cr in 2021 → ₹2,695 Cr in 2025) with no commensurate improvement in capital efficiency. FY25 net profit of ₹68 Cr is the first positive year after six years of losses; that is nowhere near enough history to validate a sustained high-ROIC franchise. At P/E 44x and EV/EBITDA 15.9x, the market is pricing in a high-quality compounder — but the underlying numbers do not support that label by any quantitative screen Greenblatt would run.
